title: A Sigil for the Wolf
premise: Mara Almeida has spent twelve years hiding her guild's last living magic behind harmless trinkets in Vharen, a city where the practice of sigilcraft is punishable by death. When a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands and names her the 'keybearer,' she learns the king of Vharen died years ago—replaced by a hollow thing sustained by a stolen binding sigil that is now devouring the city's luck, its children's health, and eventually its soul. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors and betrayed by the mentor who sold her guild out a decade ago, Mara gathers an unlikely found family—a disgraced inquisitor, a smuggler who owes her a debt, and the king's forgotten daughter—and follows the map to the guild's ruined vault. There she must choose between using the original sigil to restore the true king (and her guild's power) or unbinding it entirely, ending magic's corruption but erasing her craft forever. In the climax she chooses truth over loyalty to the dead: she unmakes the sigil, frees the hollow king into merciful oblivion, and rebuilds the guild not as keepers of power but as healers working openly in the light.
about_author: Silas Sandoval is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction, a job he describes as 'reading other people's endings so I could write my own.' He lives in a coastal city much like Vharen, where he repairs antique clocks and insists none of them are enchanted.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Establishes her daily routine selling luck-knots and fever-charms in Vharen's Nightmarket while concealing real sigilwork beneath harmless craft. Introduces the city's fear of magic after the Purges. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence; she is safe, invisible, and quietly dying inside.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A bleeding courier collapses in her shop at closing, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and whispering 'keybearer' before dying. She hides his body as inquisitor boots pass outside. Emotional beat: terror and reluctant responsibility; the past has found her.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with a flashback to her childhood in the guild. The map leads to the Hollow Vault beneath Mount Serel and bears her old master's seal—the man who vanished during the Purges. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing; the life she buried is demanding excavation.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Who Knocks Politely
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dain Ferro's POV. Ferro investigates the courier's death and interviews Mara, sensing something off but lacking proof. He is honest, weary, and increasingly doubtful of the Crown's crusade. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse with mutual respect; two decent people on collision courses.

chapters.title: Debt of Salt
chapters.summary: Smuggler Oskar Vey's POV. Mara calls in an old favor: passage out of the city. Oskar owes her for healing his sister and hates it. Emotional beat: prickly banter masking loyalty; the first thread of found family.

chapters.title: Out Through the Weir Gate
chapters.summary: Mara and Oskar's POV alternating. A tense escape through the harbor checkpoints; Mara uses a minor sigil publicly for the first time in twelve years to blind a guard. Emotional beat: exhilaration and guilt; the invisible life is officially over.

chapters.title: The Road Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On the mountain road they find villages blighted—crops failing, children gray-eyed and listless. An old woman recognizes Mara's guild mark and begs for help. Emotional beat: the cost of her long silence made visible; staying neutral was never innocent.

chapters.title: Ferro Follows
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ordered to hunt the 'keybearer' by Chancellor Rell, Ferro begins suspecting the Crown itself is rotten when his requests to examine the king are denied. Emotional beat: institutional faith cracking; duty pulling against conscience.

chapters.title: The Waystation Fire
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Inquisitor outriders ambush them at a waystation; in the chaos their fire spreads to a family's wagon. Mara saves the family's daughter, Liss, whose parents die. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt transferred; she gains a ward she never wanted.

chapters.title: Three at the Table
chapters.summary: Oskar's POV. Around a campfire, Mara teaches Liss a simple knot-charm to help her sleep. Oskar watches this makeshift family form and admits he's stopped counting the days until he can leave. Emotional beat: warmth hard-won; belonging sneaks up on the unwilling.

chapters.title: Rell's Bargain
chapters.summary: Chancellor Rell's POV. Revealed: Rell knows the king is dead and sustains the hollow replacement because order depends on it. He offers Ferro promotion to look away. Emotional beat: chilling pragmatism; the antagonist believes he is the hero.

chapters.title: The Guild Mark Burns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her guild tattoo flares whenever they near the mountain—the map responding to her blood. She confesses to Oskar that she was the guild's youngest sworn member and the only one who escaped the Purge raid. Emotional beat: confession as relief; secrets shed like bandages.

chapters.title: Hollow Men
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro encounters one of the king's 'gray guards'—men with no reflections, no pulse, serving something in the palace. He kills one and vomits afterward. Emotional beat: horror and resolve; the conspiracy is worse than treason.

chapters.title: Liss Runs
chapters.summary: Liss's POV. Frightened by a nightmare of the Vault, Liss runs off and is nearly taken by gray guards. Mara finds her using a tracking sigil, burning through her limited strength. Emotional beat: fear crystallizing into fierce protectiveness; Mara is a mother now whether she chose it or not.

chapters.title: The Pass of Teeth
chapters.summary: Oskar's POV. A treacherous mountain pass crossing; Oskar nearly dies holding a rope line and Mara drags him back. He finally tells her why he really owed her: his sister wasn't sick, she was cursed by a Crown purge-squad. Emotional beat: debts revealed as kinship; gratitude becomes love's rough cousin.

chapters.title: Letters from a Dead Master
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sheltering in a shrine, Mara deciphers marginalia on the map—her master Aldric's handwriting, written years after his supposed death. He is alive, and he warned someone would come for the keybearer. Emotional beat: hope tangled with dread; reunion may be a trap.

chapters.title: Ferro Catches Up
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro corners them at the shrine—but instead of arresting them, he shows Ferro-proof of the gray guards and asks what they know. Mara tests him with a truth-sigil. Emotional beat: trust gambled; the enemy's enemy, cautiously admitted to the fire.

chapters.title: Four at the Table
chapters.summary: Oskar's POV. The group debates turning back. Liss votes to go on. Oskar realizes he's outnumbered by people he'd die for. Emotional beat: the found family solidifies around a shared, dangerous purpose.

chapters.title: The Palace Above the Clouds
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Flashback interlude: Ferro's last audience with the king three years ago, when the monarch repeated the same sentence eleven times without blinking. Emotional beat: retroactive dread; the reader sees how long the rot has spread.

chapters.title: Aldric
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the Vault's threshold they find Aldric—aged, half-mad, keeping the outer seals alive alone for twelve years. His joy at seeing Mara curdles when he learns she brought strangers. Emotional beat: reunion shadowed by obsession; her mentor is both savior and suspect.

chapters.title: The Vault of Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Inside the Vault: thousands of sigils, each bound to a person's true name—including one labeled with the royal line. Aldric explains the Binding: the guild once anchored the kingdom's fortune to its kings, and something learned to feed on the anchor. Emotional beat: awe and revulsion; her heritage is magnificent and monstrous.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. In the capital, the hollow king unravels further—speaking in dead voices, weeping ink. Rell accelerates plans to move the Binding to a new vessel: himself. Emotional beat: ambition curdling into desperation; even the schemer is running out of time.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Price
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Aldric reveals the ritual requires a keybearer's willing sacrifice—the keybearer's own name woven into the new Binding. He raised Mara's mark on the map hoping she'd come willingly. Emotional beat: betrayal at the heart of love; loyalty weaponized.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara refuses to be a sacrifice and proposes instead to unbind the sigil entirely—freeing the kingdom from the anchor, at the cost of all guild magic, including hers. Aldric calls it murder of everything they were. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; truth over loyalty to tradition.

chapters.title: Schism at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Oskar's POV. Aldric tries to take Liss as an alternative vessel—children bind cleanly. Oskar and Ferro fight him off; Mara stops Aldric with a disabling sigil and locks him in the antechamber. Emotional beat: protective fury; the family closes ranks against its own founder.

chapters.title: Ferro's Choice
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Word arrives that Rell has declared Ferro a traitor and taken his family into custody. He must choose: return and submit, or see this through. Emotional beat: the law vs. justice distilled into one man's night of anguish.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The party descends into the Vault's heart, pursued by gray guards drawn to the disturbance. Liss proves unexpectedly gifted with knotwork, holding a ward open. Emotional beat: courage in the young; the next generation already surpassing the old.

chapters.title: Rell Arrives
chapters.summary: Rell's POV. Rell's retinue reaches the Vault simultaneously—he needs the Binding moved before the king collapses publicly. Gray guards turn on everyone. Chaos in the dark. Emotional beat: all factions colliding; the story's threads pulled taut.

chapters.title: The King Below
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They find the true king—not dead but sealed inside the Binding itself, conscious for twelve years, kept alive as the anchor's battery. He begs Mara for release, any release. Emotional beat: compassion versus strategy; mercy has a price.

chapters.title: Aldric's Last Seal
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Escaping his confinement, Aldric attempts to complete his own ritual mid-chaos. Mara confronts him with the memory of the guild's first oath: 'We serve, we do not consume.' He falters—and is killed by a gray guard saving her. Emotional beat: tragic reconciliation; the mentor's final act redeems, imperfectly.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Climax begins: Mara begins unraveling the great sigil while Rell fights Ferro and Oskar holds the corridor. Each thread she pulls costs her a memory of the guild. Emotional beat: sacrifice measured in selfhood; she pays in who she was.

chapters.title: What Mara Forgot
chapters.summary: Liss's POV. Liss watches Mara forget—her master's face, her mother's lullaby—and steps in, using Aldric's notes to hold the pattern steady. Emotional beat: inheritance in action; the student becomes the keeper.

chapters.title: The Hollow King Falls
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. With the Binding broken, the hollow thing wearing the crown collapses into dust and the true king dies peacefully in Mara's arms, whispering thanks. Rell, exposed before witnesses, is arrested by his own guards. Emotional beat: catharsis; the monster ends not in battle but in release.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Dark
chapters.summary: Oskar's POV. The survivors emerge to dawn. Mara remembers almost nothing of her guild years—only faces without names. Oskar promises to remember for her. Emotional beat: tender devastation; memory survives in the ones who love you.

chapters.title: The Kingdom Without Luck
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Weeks later: Vharen adjusts. No more anchored fortune—crops fail sometimes, people get unlucky, but children's eyes clear and the gray guards crumble. Ferro testifies before a provisional council. Emotional beat: sober hope; freedom is messier than enchantment.

chapters.title: The Empty Shop
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara returns to her Nightmarket shop, unable to work magic anymore, unsure who she is without it. Liss unpacks boxes beside her. Emotional beat: identity grief; the quiet after the storm.

chapters.title: Knots That Hold
chapters.summary: Liss's POV. Liss begins teaching neighborhood children simple knotwork—craft without binding, luck made by hand. Mara watches and realizes the guild isn't dead, only transformed. Emotional beat: renewal; legacy passed down in a new shape.

chapters.title: The Keybearer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Oskar gives Mara a ledger he's kept since the road: every memory she lost, written down as he witnessed it. She reads her own life back. Emotional beat: restoration through love; found family as the true archive.

chapters.title: A Sigil for the Wolf
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, closing chapter. One year later, the guild reopens openly as a house of craft and care, its new sigil a wolf—guardian, not predator. Mara signs the founding charter, Liss beside her, Oskar and Ferro at the door. Emotional beat: resolution and belonging; the family endures, and the city breathes free.
